title: Minimum Number of Swaps to Make the Binary String Alternating
summary: Given a binary string, determine the least number of swaps needed to make it alternating, or return -1 if impossible.
statement: Given a binary string, determine the least number of swaps needed to make it alternating, or return -1 if impossible. An alternating string has no two adjacent characters the same. Any two characters can be swapped, regardless of their position.
constraints: One swap may exchange any two positions, not only adjacent positions.
hints: An alternating string can have character counts differing by at most one.
Compare the input with each count-compatible pattern: 0101... or 1010....
Count mismatched positions and divide by two because every swap fixes one zero and one one.
When counts differ, only one pattern is possible; when equal, choosing the smaller mismatch count gives the minimum number of arbitrary swaps.
editorial: When counts differ, only one pattern is possible; when equal, choosing the smaller mismatch count gives the minimum number of arbitrary swaps.

tests.explanation: Swapping one misplaced one with one misplaced zero produces an alternating string.
The counts differ by more than one, so alternation is impossible.
